title.en: The Shapes of the Sun and Moon (Brush Talks from Dream Brook)

edition.en: Three consecutive entries from book 7 (Images and Numbers 1) of the Mengxi bitan, as given on Chinese Wikisource.
edition.zh: 《梦溪笔谈》卷七“象数一”中相连的三则，据维基文库。

basis.en: Northern Song prose; the author died in 1095.
basis.zh: 北宋散文，作者卒于 1095 年。

note.en: Three questions Shen Kuo was asked while working on the armillary sphere, and his answers: why the lunar lodges are unequal, why the sun and moon must be round, and why there is not an eclipse every month. The second answer is a small experiment anyone can repeat with a ball half covered in powder. The third describes the paths of the sun and moon as two rings laid one on another, slightly askew.
note.zh: 沈括参与详定浑仪时被问到的三个问题及其回答：二十八宿为何不均，日月为何必是圆球，为何并非每月都有日月食。第二个回答是任何人都能重复的小实验：一只半边涂粉的弹丸。第三个回答把黄道与月道比作两个相叠而略有偏差的环。

excerpt.orig: 如一彈丸，以粉塗其半，側視之，則粉處如鉤；對視之，則正圓
excerpt.en: Take a ball and coat half of it with white powder. Look at it from the side, and the powdered part is like a hook; look at it head on, and it is perfectly round.
excerpt.zh: 如一弹丸，以粉涂其半，侧视之，则粉处如钩；对视之，则正圆
